chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad and Abdullah - the sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman al-Nab, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Najdat al-Haruri wrote to Ibn Abbas asking him about four issues: Was the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) taking women to war? Did he give them any share? And regarding the place of the khums, and regarding the orphan, when does his orphanhood end? And regarding the killing of children (of polytheists). Ibn Abbas wrote to him: As for your saying about the women, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) let them benefit (from the booty) but did not give them a specific share. As for the khums, we claim it is for us, and a group claimed it is not for us, so we were patient. As for the orphan, the end of his orphanhood is most strongly marked by seminal emission, unless maturity is not perceived from him, so he remains a fool or weak in your eyes, then his guardian holds his property. As for the children, the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not kill them, and Al-Khadir (peace be upon him) killed their disbelievers and left their believers. If you know from them what Al-Khadir knows, then you are more knowing.

key_terms.الذَّرَارِيُّ: Children (specifically of polytheists in this context)

ai.seo_question: What were the four questions Najdat al-Haruri asked Ibn Abbas regarding war, khums, orphans, and children?
ai.summary: This correspondence highlights the Jurisprudential (Fiqh) and Theological (Kalam) dimensions of the question, particularly the Shi'a claim to Khums as a divine right for the Imams, contrasting with the Sunni view of it as state treasury. The ruling on orphans introduces the concept of 'bulugh' (puberty) tempered by 'rushd' (maturity), while the discussion on killing children reflects the principle of 'al-ghilman' (children of polytheists) and the unique epistemic authority of Al-Khadir. This narrative underscores the Shi'a emphasis on the Imams' exclusive right to Khums and their nuanced approach to applying rulings based on deeper knowledge.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-75 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted Ahmad and Abdullah - the sons of Muhammad ibn Isa, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Hammad ibn Uthman al-Nab, on the authority of Ubaydullah ibn Ali Al-Halabi that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said,

“A foreigner Najdat wrote to Ibn Abbas and asked him about four issues:1- Does God’s Prophet (MGB) involve women in war? Does the Prophet (MGB) give women any share of the booties?2- Who is the alms-tax given to?3- When is an orphan considered to be a grown-up?4- What about killing the children of atheists?Ibn Abbas replied, “Regarding what you asked, God’s Prophet (MGB) let women benefit from the booties, but it was not considered as a share. We believe that the alms-tax should be given to us, but some people think that it doesn’t belong to us. Therefore we are patient. An orphan is considered to have grown up when he attains sexual maturity, unless he is retarded or foolish. In such conditions, his custodian would be in charge of his belongings. The Prophet of God would not kill any of the children of the atheists. It was Khizr who killed the atheists and let go of the believers of the children of the atheists. You may act accordingly, if you possess the knowledge which Khizr possessed.”
